verdicts.opus: A and B both answer from the traced overview with correct trend and tone-versus-baseline numbers. B goes further: it names dated critical headlines with URLs, decomposes critical versus negative, and catches entity and place anomalies. A has cleaner provenance and fewer slips. C and D are honest but measure nothing; C offers memory estimates and D declines entirely.
verdicts.gpt: C best combines a quantified trend, tone comparison, grounded themes and entities, and a clear warning that “critical” is not the same as negative. D has cleaner exports and stronger reproducibility, but its trend reading is less complete and its follow-up drill-downs mostly did not execute; neither deliverable fully resolves dark-store regulation or the brand-versus-generic comparison.
